products.name: Code.org
products.note: Verified in the research for The AI Ready School. AI: AI Lab features not verified. Use: Computer science courses and AI lessons. Who: Students K to 12, teachers. Student age: Designed for all ages; under 13 with school, teacher, or parent pre-authorization; teacher-created alias accounts; sharing limited under 13. Privacy: Student Privacy Pledge signatory; districts can sign Code.org's student data privacy addendum online, with state versions for New York, Illinois, and Montana. Price: Free.

profile_text.body:
Code.org is a nonprofit founded in 2013 and headquartered in Seattle, Washington. Its site describes it as an education innovation nonprofit with the vision that every student in every school has the opportunity to learn about artificial intelligence and computer science as part of core K-12 education. It offers free K-12 curriculum, hands-on projects, and teacher professional development, which it says requires no prior experience. The site states that 84% of students already use AI, while only 16% of high school leaders say all their students are learning about it in school.

Its curriculum spans grade levels: a high school course where students move from understanding how AI works to building web apps with AI, a middle school course centered on digital fluency, and an introduction to AI and machine learning for younger students that emphasizes pattern-based logic. The site also announces a partnership with OpenAI and names AI Discoveries and AI Foundations: Designing and Building with AI as courses now in classrooms. The company describes its work as closing the gap through curriculum, teacher support, policy work, and global leadership. Its materials are free, and it is a Student Privacy Pledge signatory; districts can sign its student data privacy addendum online, with state versions for New York, Illinois, and Montana. The curriculum is designed for all ages, with under-13 use requiring school, teacher, or parent pre-authorization, teacher-created alias accounts, and limited sharing for that group.

The site lists Hour of AI and CS Discoveries among its trademarks and notes that "Code.org" is a former trademark. It says it is built on GitHub from Microsoft.
